title: Birational Riemann--Zariski compactness and affine valuation neighbourhoods
statement: Let $Z$ be an integral quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with function field $F$, the local ring at its generic point. Quasi-compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover; quasi-separated means that intersections of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. A birational model of $Z$ means an integral scheme $Z'$, a proper morphism $Z'\to Z$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and an identification $k(Z')=F$ compatible with its generic-point map; a birational quasi-model has instead a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\operatorname{Val}_F(Z)$ consist of valuation subrings $O\subseteq F$ with fraction field $F$, together with morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}O\to Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] inducing the generic-point map. A valuation subring means that for every $a\in F^\times$ either $a\in O$ or $a^{-1}\in O$. A lift to a model or quasi-model means a factorization of this morphism. Give $\operatorname{Val}_F(Z)$ the coarsest topology for which the centre projections to all birational models are continuous. Then (i) this space is quasi-compact; (ii) every birational quasi-model $U\to Z$ induces, by composition, a homeomorphism $\operatorname{Val}_F(U)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Val}_F(Z)$ onto an open subspace; (iii) for each $(O,\operatorname{Spec}O\to Z)$, its affine neighbourhoods of centres on birational models, with transition morphisms over $Z$, admit a small cofiltered indexing category, and their coordinate rings $A_j\subseteq O\subseteq F$ form a filtered diagram with injective transition maps, common fraction field $F$, and $\varinjlim_j A_j=O$. A valuation lifts uniquely to every birational model. In (iii) one may restrict to models dominating any one prescribed birational model and to affine neighbourhoods contained in any prescribed neighbourhood of its centre.

source.place: Section 3.2: Proposition 3.2.1, Lemma 3.2.2, Corollaries 3.2.4--3.2.5 and 3.2.7, pp. 15--17. Primary PDF read online on 2026-10-18; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: We use reduced generic closures throughout. If a scheme $P$ proper over $Z$ has a specified $Z$-map $\operatorname{Spec}F\to P$, take the reduced induced closed subscheme $C$ of the closure of its image, using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. It is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral. On any affine chart meeting that image its coordinate ring is the quotient by the kernel of the map to $F$. Thus the generic map factors through $C$. Its generic residue field is $F$: it embeds into $F$, while the map from $Z$ supplies the opposite inclusion $F\to k(C)$, whose composite into $F$ is the identity. So $C$ is a birational model. It is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. This construction imposes no Noetherian or finite-presentation hypothesis.

source.place: Section 3.2 opening paragraph and Lemma 3.2.3; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: The identity model $Z$ exists. Given models $X,Y$, their fibre product is proper over $Z$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Apply Step 1 to the pair of generic maps into this product. The resulting integral model dominates both. Refinement maps are unique: for two maps from an integral model to $Y$, their equalizer is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $Y/Z$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Its ideal vanishes at the generic point. The injection of every nonempty affine ring into the function field [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] forces that ideal to be zero. Consequently the equalizer is the whole source. Choosing representatives makes the model system a directed partially ordered set, ordered with dominating models larger.

source.place: Section 3.2 opening paragraph; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: This directed set can be chosen small. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] every model has a finite affine cover over a fixed finite affine cover of $Z$. Each nonempty affine ring embeds into the set $F$ by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], so its possible rings form a subset of the power set of $F$. Finite lists of these spectra, choices of their overlap opens, gluing isomorphisms, and structure morphisms to the fixed scheme $Z$ are all sets of data. Every model is represented by such data. Hence representatives of their isomorphism classes, and their morphisms, form sets. The same argument applies when affine opens of the models and a prescribed valuation centre are included in the data.

source.place: Section 3.2, indexing of all modifications; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: Every proper model is qcqs: properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2), with the qcqs base $Z$, gives both properties of its source. Each refinement is proper by [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target], hence quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral], the model spaces are spectral; refinements are spectral maps, since quasi-compactness says exactly that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Form the space $R$ of compatible points on these models with the initial topology of the projections. It is the topological inverse limit by the defining universal property of the product subspace topology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-spectral-directed-limit-spectral] to the small directed system of Steps 2--3. It makes $R$ spectral and therefore quasi-compact [def-weil-spectral-space].

source.place: Proposition 3.2.1; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: Fix a compatible point $x=(x_X)$ of $R$. Inside $F$, take $R_x=\bigcup_X\mathcal O_{X,x_X}$. These inclusions are justified by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]; refinement maps induce their inclusions because they commute with the generic maps. Their stalk maps are local. Thus the union of their maximal ideals is an ideal: sums and products can be tested at a common refinement. An element outside this union is a unit already at a stage containing it, and a member cannot become a unit later because the transition maps are local. This proves that $R_x$ is local and every stage maps locally to it. The local maps $\mathcal O_{X,x_X}\to R_x$ give morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}R_x\to X$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring], with centre $x_X$. They are compatible, since they have the same centre and the same map on the local ring of the target. In particular the identity model supplies the required morphism to $Z$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2 and Corollary 3.2.4; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: For $a\in F^\times$, map $\operatorname{Spec}F$ to $Z\times\mathbf P^1_{\mathbf Z}$ with projective coordinate $[1:a]$. This product is proper over $Z$ by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Step 1 gives its reduced generic closure $X_a$, a birational model. The two standard charts of $\mathbf P^1$ cover it by [def-nagata-affine-proj]; [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion], also with the two homogeneous coordinates interchanged, identifies their coordinates as $t=T_1/T_0$ and $s=T_0/T_1$. At $x_{X_a}$ at least one chart applies. Its coordinate has generic value $a$ or $a^{-1}$, respectively, so one of these lies in $\mathcal O_{X_a,x_{X_a}}\subset R_x$. Hence $R_x$ is a valuation subring of $F$ by the definition in the statement. Its fraction field is $F$, since for every nonzero $a$ either $a$ itself or its inverse lies in $R_x$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.3 and Corollary 3.2.4; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: Conversely a centred valuation $(O,v)$ lifts uniquely to every proper model by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension]: the given generic-point map and $v$ give its required square, and the fraction field is exactly $F$. Uniqueness makes the lifted centres compatible. Their local rings map locally into $O$, and these maps are their inclusions in $F$. Thus $O$ dominates their union $R_x$ of Step 5. Both are valuation rings of the same field by Step 6. Apply [lemma-nagata-valuation-intersection] with both fields $F$, $A=R_x$ and $B=O$, to get $O=R_x$. Conversely, the local maps of Step 5 give lifts with the originally prescribed centres, so uniqueness recovers $x$. The map back to $Z$ is recovered as well: at its centre both morphisms induce the same local inclusion into $O$, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] identifies them. We have a bijection $R\simeq\operatorname{Val}_F(Z)$ compatible with every centre projection. Both topologies are initial for those projections, hence this is a homeomorphism. Step 4 proves (i), and this step proves unique lifting.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.5; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: For the topology argument we record explicitly how composition preserves the hypotheses needed for compactification. If $A\to U$ and $U\to Z$ are separated and of finite type, their composite is of finite type by [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. Its diagonal factors as $A\to A\times_U A\to A\times_Z A$. The first map is a closed immersion by separatedness; the second is the base change of the closed diagonal of $U/Z$, so is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Their composite is a closed immersion: on affine charts the corresponding surjections of rings compose, using the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. This proves separatedness of the composite from [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Corollary 3.2.7, separated finite-type composites; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: Let $U\to Z$ be a birational quasi-model. Apply [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] over the qcqs scheme $Z$. Its compactification is an open immersion into a proper $Z$-scheme, by [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. Replace that proper scheme by the reduced closure of its generic point as in Step 1, denoted $\overline U$. It still contains $U$ as an open subscheme: restriction of the reduced closure to the reduced integral open $U$ has support all of $U$, and uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies it with $U$. Thus $\overline U$ is a birational model. The map on centred valuations induced by $U\to Z$ is injective by [lemma-nagata-separated-valuation-lift-unique]. Its image is exactly $p_{\overline U}^{-1}(U)$. Indeed a lift into $U$ composes to the unique proper lift into $\overline U$; conversely if the proper lift has closed centre in $U$, it factors through that open, because every point of a local spectrum generalizes its closed point. This image is open.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.7, open image; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: The set injection of Step 9 is continuous. For any birational $Z$-model $B$ and open $W\subseteq B$, take the reduced generic closure $B_U$ in $B\times_ZU$. It is integral with function field $F$ as in Step 1; it is proper over $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Thus it is a birational $U$-model. The centre projection to $B_U$, followed by its map to $B$, computes the restricted centre projection to $B$: both lifts into $B$ agree by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension]. Therefore the inverse image of $p_B^{-1}(W)$ is the inverse image of the open $W$ in $B_U$, an open subset of $\operatorname{Val}_F(U)$. This verifies continuity on all the generating opens of the target topology.

source.place: Corollary 3.2.7, continuity; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: For inverse continuity, let $A\to U$ be any birational model and $W\subseteq A$ open. Step 8 shows $A\to Z$ is separated of finite type, so [sk-thm-nagata-compactification] compactifies it. Its reduced generic closure $\overline A$ is a birational $Z$-model containing $A$ as an open, by the argument of Step 9 and [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Under the injection of Step 9 the generating open $p_A^{-1}(W)$ is precisely $p_{\overline A}^{-1}(W)$ intersected with the image. To check the nontrivial direction, start with a valuation in that image, lift it to $U$, then lift to $A$ by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension] for $A/U$. Its composite into $\overline A$ equals the proper $Z$-lift by the same uniqueness theorem. Thus its centre lies in $W$ exactly when its $A$-centre does. These opens generate the source topology, proving inverse continuity and hence (ii). The qcqs property required if constructing the source limit follows from finite type and separatedness of $U/Z$ and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Corollary 3.2.7, inverse continuity; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: Fix $(O,v)$ and let $c_X$ be its unique centre on every birational model. Index pairs $(X,V)$ with $V$ an affine open containing $c_X$, and arrows the $Z$-morphisms $V'\to V$ commuting with the generic maps. Such arrows are unique by the closed-diagonal argument in Step 2, since $V\to Z$ is separated (its diagonal is the restriction of that of $X/Z$). Any such arrow respects the valuation lifts: composing $\operatorname{Spec}O\to V'$ into $X$ gives the unique lift there by [lemma-nagata-proper-separated-valuation-extension]. Any two pairs have a common refinement: use the common model $Y$ of Step 2 and take an affine neighbourhood of $c_Y$ inside the intersection of the inverse images of their two opens. It maps into both. The pair category is nonempty, small by Step 3, and cofiltered; parallel-arrow equalization is automatic from uniqueness.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2, affine neighbourhood indexing; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: For every pair $(X,V=\operatorname{Spec}A)$ the whole map $\operatorname{Spec}O\to X$ factors through $V$, because $V$ contains its closed centre. The ring map $A\to O$ is injective and is its generic embedding into $F$ by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]. The fraction field of $A$ is $F$: its localization at the centre is $\mathcal O_{X,c_X}$, whose fraction field is $F$ by that node, and localization does not change the fraction field of a domain. Every transition is consequently inclusion of subrings of $O\subseteq F$. Their filtered union is $O$. Namely Step 7 gives $O=\bigcup_X\mathcal O_{X,c_X}$; if $a$ belongs to such a local ring, choose an affine neighbourhood with ring $A$ and express $a=b/s$ in $A_{\mathfrak p}$, $s\notin\mathfrak p$. The smaller affine $D(s)$ has ring $A_s$ containing $a$. Finally a directed union of subrings is their colimit: any compatible maps to another ring agree on overlaps after passing to a common stage, and hence define the unique ring map on the union. This proves every ring-diagram assertion in (iii).

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2 and Corollaries 3.2.4--3.2.5; primary PDF read online; local copy WANTED, argument written by agent

proof.text: Given a prescribed birational model $X_0$ and a neighbourhood $N$ of its centre, repeat Step 12 after restricting to models dominating $X_0$ and to affine opens contained in the inverse image of $N$. This restricted category is nonempty and cofiltered: a common refinement can first be taken with $X_0$, then one chooses an affine neighbourhood of its centre inside all the finitely many inverse-image opens. It is cofinal for the ring system, since the same procedure starts from any pair of the original category. Explicitly every element represented in a former affine ring stays represented after its inclusion into such a refined affine ring. Thus the directed union is still $O$ by Step 13, with the same injective transitions and fraction field. If a neighbourhood has been specified on a different model, first dominate that model as well. This establishes the final restriction assertion.

Existence and uniqueness of lifts through proper models, also for models over quasi-models; the unit has no generic valuative criterion.
Identify the dominating valuation O with the union valuation R_x in the same field; the unit has no generic valuation-domination theorem.
Properness of the ambient projective line for the graph that tests a versus its inverse; no same-unit projective-space theorem.
Standard projective charts and their cover, used in the graph test; this is the existing projective-spectrum construction.
Identify the two projective-line charts with affine lines and their rational coordinates; no same-unit chart theorem.
Compactify separated finite-type quasi-models over an arbitrary qcqs base; no same-unit compactification theorem.
Read the open immersion and proper factor supplied by the compactification theorem.
Injectivity for valuation lifts into a separated quasi-model; properness is not assumed for that quasi-model.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q06-5e85bdf77 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's statement (unchanged), all 14 steps and the statement of every one of the 24 proof_deps and 4 stmt_deps. The statement is the true fixed-field Riemann–Zariski result. I tested it on four cases: a field base, the trivial valuation, the line with doubled origin, where the prescribed morphism keeps two centres with the same O apart, and non-Noetherian bases. Step 1: the reduced closure is integral with k(C)=F and is proper. Step 2: the equalizer is the pullback of the closed diagonal, and its ideal is zero because sections inject into F. Step 4: the models are qcqs and the refinements are proper (triangle lemma), so the spectral directed-limit node gives (i). Steps 5–7: R_x is local, the P^1 graph shows it is a valuation ring (P(n;S)=S×P^n_Z checked), and the valuative criterion plus valuation-intersection with K=L=F give O=R_x, so the map is a homeomorphism. Step 8: separated finite-type maps compose (elementary). Steps 9–11 prove (ii) by Nagata over a qcqs base, using the reduced closure, uniqueness of separated lifts and stability of opens under generization, and both continuity directions are checked. Steps 12–14 prove (iii): arrows are unique, refinements use affine neighbourhoods inside intersections of inverse images (no claim that intersections of affines are affine), small and cofiltered, A_s shrinking gives union O, and the restrictions are cofinal. A transitive walk from the item finds no cycle (205 nodes reached). The three existing RZ nodes need a separable closure and some a finite-type base, so none is a duplicate or generalization. There are no new nodes. I accept all 11 declared tool_uses as generic tools. Temkin §3.2 is not in literature/: the WANTED entry and proof_origin=agent are correct, and I judged the proof against the cited statements. No SGA. No changes.
